Based on my chemical knowledge, I can analyze this question:

When polymerizable compounds (such as styrene, vinyl monomers, acrylates, etc.) are mixed with toxic metals or metal compounds, one of the main hazards is violent polymerization. Many metal compounds can act as catalysts that initiate or accelerate polymerization reactions. This can lead to:

1. Violent polymerization - Many metals and metal compounds can catalyze rapid, uncontrolled polymerization reactions
2. Heat generation - Polymerization reactions are typically exothermic
3. Potential for pressure build-up in closed containers
4. In some cases, this could lead to container rupture or explosion

The most direct and significant hazard when mixing polymerizable compounds with toxic metals is violent polymerization, as metals often serve as catalysts that can trigger rapid, exothermic polymerization reactions.
